find-code: Search a repository with rg (contents) and fd (file names). Use for where a symbol is defined or used, files by type, name or date, match counts, or acting on every match. Not for one simple lookup (grep/find tools) or syntax-aware matching (structural-code-search).
structural-code-search: Find or rewrite code by its syntax tree with ast-grep. Use when text search gives false hits in comments or strings, or when many call sites must change the same way. Not for plain name or text searches (find-code) or a single edit (edit tool).
code-graph-search: Explore a codebase through the graphin MCP tools. Use to find where a feature lives, who calls a function, what it depends on, or what a change would affect. Not when no mcp__graphin__ tools are available, or for exact text matches (find-code).
terminal-session-control: Run programs that need a real terminal in a psmux session. Use for REPLs, CLIs that prompt or wait for keys, TUIs, and servers you must watch or type into. Not for commands that just run to completion (bash) or long builds and tests (background tool).
json-querying: Read and change JSON with jq. Use to pull fields from JSON files or command output, filter or count records, convert to CSV, or edit a value. Not for YAML, XML or TOML, or a small JSON file you only need to view (read tool).
http-api-testing: Call and check HTTP APIs with hurl files. Use to see what an endpoint returns, reproduce an API bug, or write repeatable API tests. Not for browser pages (web-page-reading, web-page-automation) or hosts outside the internal network.
project-task-running: Find and run a project's tasks with just. Use when the project has a justfile, to find its build, test or run command, or to add a reusable task. Not for projects without a justfile (use their own build tool).
gitlab-workflow: Work with the internal GitLab through glab. Use for merge requests, reviews, issues, pipelines and CI job failures, or the GitLab API. Not for local git work (commit, branch, diff) or GitHub (github-workflow).
github-workflow: Work with GitHub or GitHub Enterprise through gh. Use for pull requests, reviews, issues, Actions runs and failed checks, or the GitHub API. Not for local git work (commit, branch, diff) or the internal GitLab (gitlab-workflow).
sql-querying: Query databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle and others) with usql and the saved connections. Use to look up data, inspect schemas, compare records, or run a .sql file. Not when mcp__dbhub__ tools can answer it, or for Oracle DDL or PL/SQL source (oracle-db-querying).
oracle-db-querying: Work with Oracle through SQLcl (sql). Use for Oracle-only needs such as object DDL, PL/SQL source, Oracle metadata, or Oracle .sql scripts. Not for plain data queries (sql-querying or mcp__dbhub__ tools) or other databases.
web-page-reading: Read internal web pages, including JavaScript-rendered ones, as text, markdown or links with obscura. Use to see what a page says or collect content from many pages. Not for clicking, typing, logins or screenshots (web-page-automation) or JSON APIs (http-api-testing).
web-page-automation: Operate internal web pages in a headless browser with agent-browser. Use to click through UI flows, submit forms, check how a page looks or behaves, or take screenshots. Not for only reading content (web-page-reading) or calling APIs (http-api-testing).
